problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+49y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{x}^{-7}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-7}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+49y=0,\,y(1)=1,\,{y}^{′}(1)=1,\,x>0.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Cauchy-Euler Equations: Characteristic Equations With Repeated Roots

feedback.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-17t{y}^{′}+81y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{t}^{9}+{c}_{2}{t}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡t,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-17t{y}^{′}+81y,\,y(1)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=3,\,t>0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=0.$ Substituting $y(1)=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=3.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =9{c}_{1}{t}^{8}+{c}_{2}{t}^{8}+9{c}_{2}{t}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=3$ and ${c}_{1}=0$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =9{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ 3 & =0+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & =3{t}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$
